question_text: Explain how backpropagation works in a neural network.
evaluation_hints: Look for understanding of the chain rule, gradient flow direction (output to input), and the role of the loss function.

question_text: What is overfitting in machine learning and how do you prevent it?
evaluation_hints: Key insight: overfitting means low training error but high test error. Prevention strategies should be specific and accurate.

question_text: What is the attention mechanism in transformers and why is it important?
evaluation_hints: Self-attention allows each token to attend to all others. Multi-head attention captures different relationship types simultaneously.

question_text: Explain the difference between batch gradient descent, stochastic gradient descent, and mini-batch gradient descent.
expected_concepts: batch uses entire dataset per update
SGD uses one sample per update
trade-off between noise and convergence speed
evaluation_hints: Focus on memory implications, convergence noise, and why mini-batch is the practical choice.

question_text: Explain how React's virtual DOM works and why it improves performance.
expected_concepts: virtual DOM is an in-memory representation
diffing algorithm compares old and new trees
only changed nodes are updated in real DOM
evaluation_hints: The key insight is that real DOM manipulation is expensive; the virtual DOM minimizes it through diffing and batching.

question_text: What is the difference between HTTP GET and POST requests?
expected_concepts: GET retrieves data, POST sends data
GET parameters in URL, POST in body
GET is idempotent, POST is not
GET can be cached, POST generally cannot
evaluation_hints: Idempotency is a key conceptual distinction. Caching and URL visibility are practical differences.

question_text: Explain the difference between Server-Side Rendering (SSR) and Static Site Generation (SSG) in Next.js.
expected_concepts: SSR: always fresh data, higher server cost
SSG: fast delivery via CDN, stale data risk
evaluation_hints: The core trade-off is data freshness vs. performance/cost. ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration) bridges the gap.

question_text: What is the difference between correlation and causation? Give an example.
expected_concepts: causation: one variable causes the other
evaluation_hints: A classic example: ice cream sales correlate with drowning rates (confound: hot weather). Experiments with random assignment establish causation.

question_text: Explain the difference between SQL and NoSQL databases and when you would choose each.
expected_concepts: SQL for complex joins and transactions
NoSQL for high write throughput or varied data shapes
evaluation_hints: The choice depends on data structure predictability, consistency requirements, and scale. Neither is universally better.
